item.title: [Feature Request] Export Copilot Plans to Local Repository for Version Control
item.body:
### Problem

When GitHub Copilot creates a plan in VS Code, it exists only in VS Code's session state and is lost when the workspace closes or cache is cleared. This prevents:

- Version control integration with git
- Building a historical record of planning decisions
- Searching/indexing plans alongside project documentation
- Referencing past plans in future development sessions

### Proposed Solution

Add a VS Code setting to automatically export plans to a configurable local folder:

```json
{
  "copilot.plan.exportPath": ".copilot-plans",
  "copilot.plan.autoExport": true
}
```

### Expected Behavior

- Plans are automatically saved as markdown files with timestamps
- Each plan includes metadata (creation time, title, model used)
- Users can opt-in via settings
- Plans are git-trackable for team collaboration
- Users can also manually export plans via the command palette

### Use Case

In a RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) system for business operations, saved plans become indexable documents that can inform future development, provide audit trails, and enable knowledge retention across sessions and team members.

Without this feature, the only workaround is manually copying plan content into version-controlled markdown files, which is tedious and easy to forget.

### Example Generated Files

```
.copilot-plans/
  2026-03-06T143022-implement-export-feature.md
  2026-03-06T091547-refactor-database-schema.md
```

Each file would contain the plan content plus frontmatter metadata:

```yaml
---
created: 2026-03-06T14:30:22
title: Implement export feature
model: claude-opus-4-20250514
session: abc123
---
```

comments.body:
I particularly miss a feature to export the chat content as @adambraimbridge describes.

Question for the VS Code team: Should this feature also export chat content too, or should chat exporting be a separate but related feature?

It would be nice to have a Markdown document containing all the chat content that could be reused elsewhere.
